hint.system: Switch to system mode (the OS decides whether light or dark mode)

current.system: System mode: the OS decides whether light or dark mode

home.title: Welcome
home.intro: MixTape is a music and audiobook collection running on a private home server — not a streaming service, but real files, gathered over years.
home.invite: Accounts are by invitation only. A shared link needs none — it simply plays.

login.title: Sign in
login.twoFactorHint: Two-factor authentication is enabled for your account. Please check your app and enter the one-time code shown there.
login.helpLinksLabel: If you can't sign in, use these links.

register.title: Registration
register.introHint: After registering, we'll send you a link to confirm your email address. You can only sign in once your email address has been confirmed.
register.passwordHint: As you type, we check whether your password is strong enough. Weak passwords are rejected.

forgot.title: Trouble signing in?
forgot.introHint: If you can't sign in, we can send you either your username or a link to reset your password. Choose password or username, and enter the email address on file. If you've forgotten your password, you also need to provide your username.
forgot.helpLinksLabel: If you can't sign in, use these links.

reset.title: Reset password
reset.introHint: Enter your new password. After saving, you can sign in with the new password.

resend.title: Resend confirmation link
resend.introHint: If your confirmation link has expired, you can request a new link to confirm your email address here. Please provide your username and email address.

profile.headline: Update profile
profile.intro: You can change your email address and/or your username. If you change your email address, you must confirm the new address — we'll send you a confirmation link.

password.headline: Change password
password.intro: You can change your password by entering your current password and the new password.

delete.headline: Delete account
delete.explanation: You can delete your account here if necessary. {warning} — this action deletes your account and all associated data.
delete.noSoftDeletes: We don't use a “deleted” flag — the account is removed immediately and permanently.
delete.reversed: This action cannot be undone — we cannot restore deleted accounts.

modal.intro: Are you sure you want to permanently delete your account?

disabled.intro: Two-factor authentication uses {totp}. You need a compatible app, e.g. Google/Microsoft Authenticator or {bitwarden} / {enpass}.
disabled.confirm: Your password is required to enable it.

enabled.headline: Disable two-factor authentication
enabled.intro: Enter your password to disable two-factor authentication.

modal.introSetup: To finish setting up 2FA, scan the QR code in your authenticator app, or enter the setup code manually.
modal.introVerify: Enter the one-time password from your app and click “Confirm”.

recoveryCodes.headline: Recovery codes
recoveryCodes.intro: Recovery codes let you sign in when you no longer have access to your 2FA device. Store the recovery codes in a secure password manager.
recoveryCodes.usage: Each recovery code can be used only once to sign in to your account and is removed after use. If you need more recovery codes, use the “Regenerate” button.

errors.qrCode: The QR code could not be loaded.
errors.setupKey: The setup code could not be loaded.
errors.recoveryCodesLoad: The recovery codes could not be loaded.
errors.recoveryCodesRegenerate: The recovery codes could not be regenerated.

shares.headline: Your shared content
shares.summary: You have shared something as a listening link. Here you can see what is shared right now — and withdraw individual links.
shares.title: Your listening links
shares.intro: Each link works for seven days. Whoever has one can listen — with no account. Revoke a link and it stops working immediately.
shares.expiredIntro: These links no longer work. Click “expired” to switch one back on — the same link, for another seven days. 30 days after expiring they disappear on their own.
shares.empty: You are not sharing anything right now.

revoke.label: Revoke the link to “{name}”
revoke.body: Do you really want to revoke the link to “{name}”? Whoever has the link will not be able to use it any more.

renew.open: Switch it back on — another seven days
renew.label: Re-activate the link to “{name}”
renew.body: The link to “{name}” will work again — for seven days from now. It is the same link as before: anybody who still has it can listen again.

tip.popular_playsThenDuration: Popular — the ones you have played most, then the most minutes
tip.popular_plays: Popular — the ones you have played most

hint.songs: Number of music files in the collection
hint.size: Combined size of all music files on disk
hint.playtime: Combined duration of all music files
hint.years: From the oldest to the newest year your albums carry — albums with no year are not counted
hint.artists: Number of artists with at least one track
hint.genres: Number of genres with at least one track

song.ownTip: How often you have played this song. It counts once half the track has been heard — after four minutes for a long one. Repeats count separately. It means this file: the same recording on another album is counted there.
song.othersTip: How often everybody else has played this song, put together — counted the same way as yours.

artist.ownTip: How often you have played this artist's songs. Each song counts once half of it has been heard — after four minutes for a long one — so playing an album twice through counts twice.
artist.othersTip: How often everybody else has played this artist's songs, put together — counted the same way as yours.

genre.ownTip: How often you have played songs in this genre. Each song counts once half of it has been heard — after four minutes for a long one. Repeats count too.
genre.othersTip: How often everybody else has played songs in this genre, put together — counted the same way as yours.

album.ownTip: How often you have played this album's songs. Each song counts once half of it has been heard — after four minutes for a long one. It means this record's own tracks: the same recording on another album counts there.
album.othersTip: How often everybody else has played this album's songs, put together — counted the same way as yours.

playlist.ownTip: How often you have played songs from this playlist. Each song counts once half of it has been heard — after four minutes for a long one. It means the songs that are in the list now: take one out and its plays stop counting here.
playlist.othersTip: How often everybody else has played songs from this playlist, put together — counted the same way as yours.

share.revoke: You can revoke it early at any time from your dashboard.
share.bearer: Anyone holding the link can listen — no account needed. Only pass it on to people you trust.
share.copyHint: Click the field to copy the link.
share.failed: The link could not be created.
share.tooMany: That is a lot of links in a short time. Try again in a moment.

discography.empty: No albums are credited to this artist.

tabs.label: This genre's albums, artists and songs

artists.label: {total} artists with this as their main genre

genre.noArtists: No artist has this as their main genre.

subjectMenu.enqueued: 1 track added to the queue. | {count} tracks added to the queue.

hint.books: Number of audiobooks in the collection
hint.chapters: Number of chapters across every audiobook
hint.size: Combined size of all chapter files on disk
hint.authors: Number of authors with at least one chapter
hint.narrators: Number of narrators with at least one chapter
hint.years: From the oldest to the newest year your audiobooks carry — books with no year are left out

playlists.reorderHint: Drag to reorder – or click it, then {keys}

detail.label: Tracks in this playlist
detail.empty: This playlist is still empty. You add tracks to it from wherever you are listening — a song or album page.
detail.reorderHint: Drag to reorder – or click it, then {keys}

export.tooltip: Downloads this playlist as an .m3u file — a list of the file paths in this order, to play in another player, on a phone or in the car. Optionally extended, with artist, title and length per entry.
export.intro: An .m3u file to take with you — for another player, a phone or a car stereo. It holds the tracks in this order; it plays wherever the music files live.
export.formatSimpleHint: Just the file paths, one line per track. Every player understands it — but the device shows whatever the files are named.
export.formatExtendedHint: Adds #EXTINF lines with artist, title and length, so the player shows the names as they read here — if it supports the format.
export.encodingUtf8Hint: For everything modern: Mac, phone, VLC. Handles every character your collection contains.
export.encodingWindowsHint: For older devices that render UTF-8 as gibberish — a car stereo, say. Characters outside Western Europe become “?”.
export.prefixHint: Put in front of every path — where the music lives as far as the device playing the file is concerned. Leave empty for relative paths.
export.unplayable: 1 track contains a character Windows-1252 cannot carry — its path will not be found on the device: {named}. Characters: {characters}. | {count} tracks contain characters Windows-1252 cannot carry — their paths will not be found on the device: {named}. Characters: {characters}.

sort.tooltip: Sorts the tracks by file path — by folder and file name, the way they sit on the disk. Puts an album back into its own order.
sort.already: The playlist is already sorted by file path.

empty.headline: No playlists yet
empty.text: A playlist is your own running order across the collection — music and audiobook chapters mixed however you like. Create your first one, then add tracks to it from any song or album page.

form.nameHint: Only you can see it — but no two of your playlists may share a name.
form.descriptionHint: Optional. What is this playlist for?
form.createIntro: The playlist starts empty. You add tracks to it afterwards, from wherever you are listening — a song or album page.
form.editIntro: This playlist's name and description. The tracks in it are left untouched.

add.song: Add this song to a playlist
add.album: Add this album to a playlist
add.artist: Add this artist to a playlist
add.genre: Add this genre to a playlist
add.label: Playlist
add.exhausted: Already in every one of your playlists.
add.duplicatesHint: Tracks already in there are skipped.

intro.album: Somebody sent you this {kind} as a listening link. You can play it right here — no account, no signing in.
intro.artist: Somebody sent you this {kind} as a listening link. You can listen right here — no account, no signing in.
intro.playlist: Somebody sent you this {kind} as a listening link. You can play it right here — no account, no signing in.
intro.audiobook: Somebody sent you this {kind} as a listening link. You can listen right here — no account, no signing in.

share.notKept: Nothing on this page is kept: the queue and your place in it start over every time the link is opened. With an account of your own both are remembered — ask whoever sent you this link for an invite.

expires.label: Link works until
expires.description: After that this link stops working. Just ask for a new one.

expired.title: This link has expired
expired.body: A listening link works for seven days. Ask whoever sent it to you for a new one – it is one click at their end.

search.label: Search the collection
search.empty: Nothing in the collection matches that.
search.failed: The search did not answer. Please try again.
search.found: One group of results, reachable with the arrow keys. | {count} groups of results, reachable with the arrow keys.

datatable.search_in_name_hint: Searching the name only — click to search everywhere (artist, album, genre too).

queue.label: Play queue
queue.moveHint: Drag to reorder — or click it, then {keys}

saveFailed.browser: The queue can no longer be saved in this browser — its storage is full or blocked. Playback continues, but the queue may not survive a restart.
saveFailed.server: The queue could not be synced to the server. It stays saved in this browser, but it will not follow you to another device for now.

queue.addIntro: The one queued track will be added to a playlist. | All {count} queued tracks will be added to a playlist.

error.unavailable: “{name}” cannot be played — the file is unavailable.
error.network: “{name}” could not be loaded — the connection was interrupted.

nowPlaying.empty: Nothing is playing. Start something from the music collection or a playlist.
